title: Mass: Converting Grams and Kilograms with Decimals
seo_title: Grade 6 Mass Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Estimate, measure, record, compare and order objects using measuring instruments; use grams (g) and kilograms (kg); calculate and solve problems involving mass, including problems with decimal fractions to 2 decimal places; convert between grams and kilograms, including conversions with decimal fractions.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 6 mass worksheets: grams and kilograms, converting with decimals, comparing masses and problems. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • 1 kg = 1 000 g.
  • To change kg to g, multiply by 1 000: 2,35 kg = 2 350 g.
  • To change g to kg, divide by 1 000: 750 g = 0,75 kg.
  • Change to the same unit before you compare, add or subtract.

Examples

Example

1,2 kg + 650 g

1,2 kg = 1 200 g

1 200 + 650

Answer: 1 850 g

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
100 g in a kg1 kg = 1 000 g.
The comma the wrong waykg is bigger, so the number is smaller.
Different unitsChange to grams first.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 6 say about mass?
faq.a: Estimate, measure, compare and order masses in g and kg, solve problems and convert between units, including with decimal fractions.

faq.q: Which is heavier, 1,5 kg or 1 450 g?

faq.a: A kitchen scale or a bathroom scale.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for the mass of a watermelon?
items.e: A watermelon is heavy to carry but far lighter than a car, so kilograms fit. 4,5 g is lighter than one 20c coin, and 4,5 t is heavier than a big car.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for the mass of a loaded truck?
items.e: A loaded truck is very heavy, so use tonnes. 12,5 t = 12 500 kg.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for the mass of an adult lion?
items.e: An adult lion is about as heavy as a big bag of dog food, so kilograms fit. 0,9 kg = 900 g, which is lighter than a carton of milk.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for the mass of a Grade 6 learner?
items.e: Most Grade 6 learners have a mass of about 30 kg to 50 kg. 3,8 kg is the mass of a new baby.

items.q: A bag of rice has a mass of 1 650 g. Which shows this in kilograms?
items.e: 1 kg = 1 000 g, so divide by 1 000: 1 650 ÷ 1 000 = 1,65 kg. (16,5 kg divides by 100, as if 1 kg were 100 g.)

items.q: Which shows 3 kg 250 g using one unit?
items.e: 250 g = 0,25 kg, so 3 kg 250 g = 3,25 kg (or 3 250 g). 325 g joins the digits and loses the 0.

items.q: Which unit would you use to measure the mass of a slice of cheese?
items.e: A slice of cheese is measured in g.

items.e: A Grade 5 learner is about 35 kg.

items.e: 34 of 1 000 g = 1 000 ÷ 4 × 3 = 750 g.

items.q: Convert 2 kg 240 g to g.
Convert. 750 g = ☐ kg
items.e: 1 kg = 1 000 g. Grams are smaller than kilograms, so divide by 1 000: 750 ÷ 1 000 = 0,75. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 750 g = 0,75 kg.

items.q: Convert. 2,375 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1 000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1 000: 2,375 × 1 000 = 2 375. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 2,375 kg = 2 375 g.

items.q: Convert. 45 g = ☐ kg
items.e: 1 kg = 1 000 g. Grams are smaller than kilograms, so divide by 1 000: 45 ÷ 1 000 = 0,045. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 45 g = 0,045 kg.

items.q: Convert. 4,08 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1 000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1 000: 4,08 × 1 000 = 4 080. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 4,08 kg = 4 080 g.

items.q: Convert. 3 kg 50 g = ☐ kg
items.e: 50 g = 50 ÷ 1 000 = 0,05 kg. So 3 kg 50 g = 3,05 kg. 3,5 kg would be 3 kg 500 g.

items.q: Work out 1,5 kg + 700 g. Give your answer in kilograms.
items.e: Use one unit first: 700 g = 0,7 kg. Then 1,5 + 0,7 = 2,2 kg. 701,5 kg adds the numbers without converting.

items.q: Which is the heaviest?
items.e: Change them all to grams: 1,2 kg = 1 200 g, 0,95 kg = 950 g, 1 kg 150 g = 1 150 g. 1 200 g is the heaviest.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of flour. What is the mass in kilograms?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 5 equal spaces, so each mark is 1 ÷ 5 = 0,2 kg (200 g). The needle is 2 marks past 1 kg: 1 + 0,4 = 1,4 kg. (1,2 kg counts each mark as 0,1 kg.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a parcel. What is the mass in kilograms?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 4 equal spaces, so each mark is 1 ÷ 4 = 0,25 kg (250 g). The needle is 3 marks past 2 kg: 2 + 0,75 = 2,75 kg. (2,3 kg counts each mark as 0,1 kg.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of some apples. What is the mass in kilograms?
items.e: The needle points to 600 g. 1 kg = 1 000 g, so divide by 1 000: 600 ÷ 1 000 = 0,6 kg.

items.q: Convert. 2,5 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1 000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1 000: 2,5 × 1 000 = 2 500. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 2,5 kg = 2 500 g. (250 g multiplies by 100, but 1 kg is 1 000 g, not 100 g.)

items.q: Convert. 2,4 t = ☐ kg
items.e: 1 t = 1 000 kg. Tonnes are bigger than kilograms, so multiply by 1 000: 2,4 × 1 000 = 2 400. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 2,4 t = 2 400 kg. (240 kg multiplies by 100, but 1 t is 1 000 kg.)

items.q: Convert. 3 500 kg = ☐ t
items.e: 1 t = 1 000 kg. Kilograms are smaller than tonnes, so divide by 1 000: 3 500 ÷ 1 000 = 3,5. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 3 500 kg = 3,5 t.

items.q: Convert. 0,6 t = ☐ kg
items.e: 1 t = 1 000 kg. Tonnes are bigger than kilograms, so multiply by 1 000: 0,6 × 1 000 = 600. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 0,6 t = 600 kg.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of flour. What is the mass in kilograms?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 5 equal spaces, so each mark is 1 ÷ 5 = 0,2 kg (200 g). The needle is 2 marks past 1 kg: 1 + 0,4 = 1,4 kg. (1,2 kg counts each mark as 0,1 kg.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a parcel. What is the mass in kilograms?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 4 equal spaces, so each mark is 1 ÷ 4 = 0,25 kg (250 g). The needle is 3 marks past 2 kg: 2 + 0,75 = 2,75 kg. (2,3 kg counts each mark as 0,1 kg.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of some apples. What is the mass in kilograms?
items.e: The needle points to 600 g. 1 kg = 1 000 g, so divide by 1 000: 600 ÷ 1 000 = 0,6 kg.

items.q: 15 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 15 of 1 000 g = 1 000 ÷ 5 = 200 g.
8 000 g = 8 kg, with 160 g left: 8 kg 160 g.
